verdict.line: You lose if you let Renekton dump his full stun combo on you for free before level 6; you win if you trade through his cooldowns and scale past his all-in window.

brief.thesis: Illaoi wins this lane 60.4% of the time over 53 games because Renekton's entire early threat is tied to a 300-range W (Ruthless Predator) on a 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown — when it's down, he has no stun and no way to stop E (Test of Spirit) from shredding his spirit. The matchup flips hard at level 6, where Renekton's Fury engine and R (Dominus) let him force fights you can't dodge, so your entire job before then is denying free W punishes while banking spirit damage.

tell.watch: Renekton's Fury bar and W cooldown

theirWindow.when: W (Ruthless Predator) off cooldown, Fury above 50
theirWindow.what: He can land a 3-hit stun that shreds shields and deals high physical damage, then follow with empowered Q (Cull the Meek) to heal off the trade. Back off to 400+ range and don't let him walk up for the first hit.

yourWindow.when: His W just went on cooldown (he used it to engage or farm)
yourWindow.what: Walk in and E (Test of Spirit, 900 range) immediately — he has no stun to punish you with for up to 16 seconds, and the spirit echoes damage back at him even if he flashes away. Follow with W (Harsh Lesson) to leap in and trigger Tentacle swings on the spirit.

powerCurve.note: Neither W nor E (yours) online yet, trade with autos only
E is up, his W still single-hit, punish cooldowns hard
Dominus online, Fury stacks faster, his all-in wins
Black Cleaver/Iceborn coming online evens trades back
Sterak's Gage plus Tentacle scaling outlasts his Fury burst

start.why: 65.9% win rate over 44 games — the lifesteal from autos matters because every E punish window is an auto-attack trade, not a spell trade.

boots.why: 76.9% is the raw number on Mercury's Treads but Steelcaps carry the sample (56.4% over 55 games) — the flat damage reduction blunts his triple-slash W and his empowered autos during Fury spikes.

core.why: 42% of games build this first in the 76.2%-winrate path — the armor shred compounds with Tentacle hits and lets your autos keep pace with his sustain.
Second item in the dominant path — the slow from the proc keeps him inside E range after he tries to dash out with E (Slice and Dice).
Third item across all three listed paths — the shield and tenacity directly counter his level-6-plus all-in where he's trying to lock you down with Dominus-empowered W.

situational.when: he's building into true damage or you need more sustain against his Q healing
he's stacking lifesteal or healing off Q (Cull the Meek) too consistently
you need an early grievous wounds answer to his Q sustain before Thornmail is ready

runes.keystoneWhy: 44.8% pick rate and the safer of the two pages — Grasp's proc-and-heal rewards the slow auto trades you're forced into when his W is down, and the extra max HP blunts his burst once Dominus comes online.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 65.7% of games and posts the best win rate (59.1%) — Teleport lets you reset after even trades and still make it back for the level-6 window where you need to not be caught out of position.

playing.title: Hold E until his W is down
playing.detail: Test of Spirit has a 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown and 900 range — use it the instant his Ruthless Predator goes on cooldown so he can't stun you out of the channel.

playing.title: Don't walk up when Fury is above 50
playing.detail: His Q and W both get bonus damage and extra effects past 50 Fury, including a third slash on W that strips shields — bait the swing from max auto range instead.

playing.title: Leap with W only after E lands
playing.detail: Harsh Lesson's 400-range leap triggers nearby Tentacles to swing at the same target as your E spirit, stacking damage he has no way to interrupt without his own stun up.

playing.title: Respect level 6 as a full stop
playing.detail: Dominus grants bonus health and periodic Fury generation — do not initiate trades here unless your Tentacles are already active from a prior E or Q.

playing.title: Track his E (Slice and Dice) for disengage
playing.detail: The 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s dash lets him reset neutral after a bad trade — if you've already applied E's spirit mark, the echo damage still ticks even if he dashes away.

playing.title: Prioritize Black Cleaver into Iceborn for lane
playing.detail: The armor shred and slow both answer his post-6 burst directly, and this order wins 76.2% in the measured sample versus reversing it.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner spells here are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win-condition reasoning and timing calls are my own read of the ability kits, not sourced from OP.GG's tips beyond the one quoted.

stats.opponentTip: Rather than engaging in first, use your [E] when he uses his (E) to brawl. Even if Renekton deals his full combo and falls back with (E), deal damage to his spirit from [E] to fight back. However, Renekton has the upper hand after reaching level 6 and without proper items, so we advise not overreaching until then.
